title: Choose the replayable local-first architecture over the hosted-control-plane alternative

problem_spec.request: Design the best architecture for a local-first decision engine that orchestrates model calls, persists search state to disk, and needs a clean path to later sync across machines.
constraints: The first release must run locally on developer laptops.
State must stay replayable and inspectable with normal filesystem tools.
success_criteria: Keep the first milestone simple enough to ship in weeks.
Preserve a credible path to collaboration and replay later.

objective.name: best_overall
objective.description: Choose the architecture that best balances local-first constraints, replayability, tractability, and future sync headroom.

candidate.thesis: Filesystem-backed append-only run journal with deferred sync
candidate.mechanism: Keep run state in explicit JSON artifacts on disk, append immutable step records locally, and add a later sync adapter that ships those artifacts between machines without changing the first local runtime.
assumptions: A small team can ship explicit filesystem state faster than a full networked control plane.
failure_modes: Future sync needs careful conflict policy.
unknowns: Which artifact granularity makes later sync easiest?
candidate.implementation_shape: Start with explicit JSON files and immutable run logs, then layer sync metadata later.
evidence: The brief prioritizes local execution, replayability, and inspectable state.

hidden_dependencies: Eventually needs a clear merge strategy once multiple machines edit the same run.
kill_shots: Breaks down if artifact structure becomes too ad hoc for later sync.
sharp_edges: Can accumulate too many small files without disciplined layout.
critique.summary: The architecture is strong, but future sync needs intentional boundaries.

candidate.thesis: Hosted orchestration control plane with local cache replicas
candidate.mechanism: Centralize run orchestration in a hosted service, mirror snapshots to local caches for speed, and treat the laptop client as a synchronized replica of the control plane.
assumptions: The team can stand up reliable hosted orchestration early without slowing the first milestone.
strengths: Offers a clean eventual collaboration story if the service exists.
failure_modes: Adds operational surface area before the first local product is proven.
unknowns: How much hosted complexity appears before the local experience is stable?
candidate.implementation_shape: Build the service first, then keep local caches in sync with it.
evidence: A central service could help collaboration later, but it is not required by the first milestone.

hidden_dependencies: Requires service reliability, authentication, and sync semantics before the first release is usable.
kill_shots: Misses the small-team simplicity target if hosted orchestration becomes the critical path.
sharp_edges: Can obscure filesystem replay if the real state of record lives remotely.
critique.summary: The hosted-first plan adds future-oriented upside, but it weakens the first milestone.

expected_assessment.summary: The append-only filesystem journal wins because it directly satisfies the local-first and replayability constraints while still leaving a disciplined path to later sync.
decisive_advantages: Better first-milestone tractability without compromising inspectable state.
Stronger evidence that the runtime can stay local and replayable from day one.
decisive_risks: Later sync still needs a merge policy.
